# Journal — job C2c (console)

## 14:48 Start
Read BRIEF, pages.json and reference tiles for console-creation-center and console-deployments.

## 14:50 Setup (~15 min)
- Vite vue-ts scaffold, three tarballs as file: deps, vue-router. `npx @aziontech/webkit init --yes` wired webkit.css, icons, eslint/stylelint, husky, .claude skills/rules, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, .mcp.json. Worked well, dry-run plan was clear.
- **medium** — dependency mismatch: webkit 5.12.0 declares `@aziontech/theme ^4.0.0` but the supplied theme tarball is 5.2.2, so npm nests a second copy (theme 4.3.1) under `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/node_modules`. Two theme versions now live in the tree; unclear which one `webkit.css` -> `@import '@aziontech/theme'` resolves (the app's 5.2.2). Neither README nor `init` mentions it; `doctor` to check later.
- **low** — `init` overwrites nothing but adds devDeps as `latest` (eslint, stylelint, husky…) and a `prepare: husky` script, which fails without a git repo; had to `git init` before `npm install`.
- **low** — docs contradict each other on the entry import: skill `webkit-usage` "App entry" says `import '@aziontech/theme'`, CLAUDE.md fragment says import `webkit.css`, never `@aziontech/theme` bare. Followed init (webkit.css).
- **low** — skill `webkit-usage` "Import + tokens" example puts `class="bg-(--primary) ..."` on `<Button>`, which the invariant "Never restyle a webkit component" forbids.
- **low** — `Link` takes `href` only (no router `to`); used `href` for the index page (full reload navigation).
- Worked well: `webkit search` found exactly the right blocks first try — `platform/create/create-hub` ("The Creation Center…" — it is literally this page), `platform/view/table-view` and `shells/console`. `add --with-guidelines` copied them and printed the route.

## 14:52 console-creation-center (~20 min)
- Started from `npx @aziontech/webkit add platform/create/create-hub`. The Default variant **is** this screen: creation header (back IconButton, Brand, Breadcrumb, Avatar), large PageHeader with file/folder buttons, dashed EmptyState card with Continue with GitHub + Manage connected providers, Filter + faded ScrollArea template gallery (3-col Recommended, 2-col lists with vendor). First shot was already the reference's layout; after content changes the desktop capture is 2782 px tall, exactly the reference's height. Excellent — this is what a block should be.
- Changed only content: H1, "choose a file or a folder", "Choose a Git provider…", "Start from Template", avatar "MY", and the three gallery sections (Recommended / Azion Templates / All Frameworks, 39 templates, copy verbatim from pages.json — generated by `scripts/gen_templates.py`).
- **low** — the block's demo copy disagrees with the reference product copy and with its own guidelines: guidelines' microcopy says "select rather than choose" and "no em dash", but the real console uses "choose" and em dashes ("Deploy a Preact app — the React API…"). Kept the reference copy verbatim.
- **medium** — no coloured Azion mark in `@aziontech/icons` (`ai-azion` exists only monochrome; `azionicons-color.css` has no `ai-cor ai-azion`). The reference shows the orange Azion glyph on every "by Azion" template. Used `ai ai-azion` + `text-(--primary)`; to do so I had to add a `tone` field and move `text-(--text-default)` from the static class into the binding, because the block hard-codes the icon colour (a small structural edit to a copied block). No icon either for Qwik colour, Nitro, Stencil, Rust/WASM, Emscripten, Cosmic, so the block's own fallbacks (`pi pi-server`, `pi pi-code`, `pi pi-microchip`) were kept.
- **low** — file / folder in the description: the block uses raw `<button class="text-link">` (underlined); the reference shows them blue and not underlined. Kept the block (it is a keyboard path to a file picker, and `Link` only renders an anchor with `href`).
- **low** — iPhone: `EmptyState` #actions stretches Continue with GitHub to full width; reference keeps it content-width. No prop on EmptyState to change this; left as is.
- **high** — TypeScript: `npm run build` (`vue-tsc -b && vite build`) failed on a fresh `create-vite vue-ts` app: every `@aziontech/webkit/<name>` import is "Cannot find module" (exports point at raw `.vue` files, no `.d.ts`), `@aziontech/icons` side-effect import has no types, and the copied blocks are JS SFCs (`<script setup>` without `lang="ts"`) so TS7016 on the router imports. README claims "vue-tsc --noEmit checks it under strict" — not true here. Fix: `allowJs` + `vueCompilerOptions.htmlAttributes: []` (from README) + my own `src/env.d.ts` with ambient `declare module '@aziontech/webkit/*'` / `'*.vue'` / `'@aziontech/icons'` shims. Loses WebKit prop typing in my TS files. Cost ~10 min.
- **low** — pre-commit hook added by `init` fails on the Vite scaffold's own `// https://vite.dev/config/` comment in vite.config.ts (`webkit/authoring-standards` bans comments in app code, which is surprisingly strict for a consumer project).
- **medium** — lint config from `init` does not ignore `dist/`: after the first `npm run build`, the husky pre-commit (`eslint .` + `stylelint "**/*.{css,scss,vue}"`) fails with 5 ESLint + 521 stylelint errors, all in the built bundle (WebKit's own compiled CSS/JS contains hex/hsl). Added `ignores: ['dist/**']` to eslint.config.mjs and a `.stylelintignore`. ~8 min (stylelint's output was not obvious behind eslint's).

## 14:58 console-deployments (~35 min)
- Built from two blocks: `shells/console` (variant ListPage: Sidebar + Menu nav, GlobalHeader with SearchTrigger/Command palette, orange Create, ButtonHighlight Agent, avatar, footer account menu, and the list toolbar Filter · search Input · Refresh · Download CSV · Columns) and `platform/view/table-view` (PageHeader + data-driven `TableRoot` bound to `useCollection`, cell presets). The shell's own placeholder toolbar matched the reference exactly, so I kept it, moved PageHeader + TableRoot + useCollection in from table-view, then deleted the unused TableView copy. The first shot already matched the reference at desktop (1136 px tall, same as the reference). Worked very well.
- Used: `Tag` (info, small, `pi pi-arrow-circle-up` = "Current"; secondary rounded small = environment), `StatusIndicator` (success/danger; `loading` gives the Building spinner), `Table.CellLink` (workload + 12px external mark), `Table.CellTime` (Deployed), `Table.CellActions`, `Avatar`, `EmptyState` for no match, and the built-in pagination footer ("Showing 1 to 10 of 71 entries", pager, rows-per-page select), which came free with useCollection. 71 mock rows, first 10 verbatim.
- **low**: product icons (`ai-workloads`, `ai-edge-application`, `ai-edge-functions`, `ai-waf-rules`, `ai-real-time-*`…) exist in @aziontech/icons and match the reference sidebar, but nothing maps a product name to its icon. I guessed the names from the class list in `dist/azionicons.css`.
- **medium**: guidance conflicts with the real console in three places on this screen. (1) Skill `webkit-tables` says "Deployed"/"Last modified" is one `Table.CellTime` column with the author avatar and "never a separate Author column", but the reference has separate "Last Editor" (avatar + name) and "Deployed" columns. I followed the reference: Avatar + name in a plain cell, CellTime without author. (2) The skill says "one chip per row"; the reference has two (Current + Environment). (3) Narrow boxes: the skill says stacked cards and that `:stackable="false"` is "never just to avoid the cards", but the console reference scrolls the table sideways with the first column + kebab visible. I used `:stackable="false"` to match the reference.
- **medium**: `StatusIndicator` with `loading` appends its own "…" to the label, so passing the reference copy "Building..." rendered "Building......". status-indicator.md doesn't document this; it only says "Shows loading state". I passed "Building" instead. ~3 min.
- **medium**: the table-view block hard-codes avatar photos from `ca.slack-edge.com` (an external network call at runtime, and photos of real people). The brief forbids runtime network calls, so Avatar shows initials; the reference shows photos. WebKit ships no local/mock avatar asset.
- **low**: iPhone: `Pagination` collapses to "‹ 1 ›" in the narrow card; the reference shows "‹ 1 2 3 4 5 … 8 ›". No prop keeps the page numbers.
- **low**: iPhone: the collapsed `SearchTrigger` draws a 44 px touch-size square while the other header IconButtons are 32 px (in the reference all are 32 px).
- **low**: on iPhone the shell toolbar wraps its icon buttons to a second line (`flex-wrap` + `min-w-36` on the search); the reference keeps one line. I changed only my own wrapper classes (no wrap, `min-w-0`).
- **low**: the breadcrumb sits in the shell's `v-else`, so a first-level page with no crumb needed a template change (`v-else-if="crumbs.length"`).
- **low**: `webkit check` reports my TS ambient `declare module '@aziontech/webkit/*'` shim as an unknown import (ERROR). I worked around it by making my two small SFCs plain JS (like the blocks), so no webkit shim is needed. `check`/`doctor` also never noticed the nested theme 4.3.1 copy.
- **low**: `webkit check` reports no block drift even though both copied blocks were heavily edited (`diff` shows it, `check` stays green); "blocks drifting from the canonical copy" in the README did not surface anything.
- **low** — `Link` ignores default-slot text and renders its built-in "Learn more" + external icon unless `label` and `:show-icon="false"` are passed (found on the index page). (14:59)

# DONE — job C2c (console)

## Pages
- `console-creation-center`: **built**. From block `platform/create/create-hub`; desktop capture 2782 px tall, same as the reference; all 39 templates with verbatim copy. Small gaps: the Azion mark is monochrome `ai-azion` tinted with `--primary` (no coloured Azion icon); file/folder links are underlined (block's `text-link` buttons); on iPhone Continue with GitHub is full-width; a few framework glyphs (Nitro, Stencil, Rust, Emscripten) are generic PrimeIcons.
- `console-deployments`: **built**. From `shells/console` + `platform/view/table-view`; desktop 1136 px, same as the reference; iPhone 889 vs 873 px. Small gaps: Last Editor avatars show initials, not photos (the block's photos are external Slack URLs, which would be runtime network calls); on iPhone the pager collapses to "‹ 1 ›"; the search icon button on iPhone is 44 px instead of 32 px.
- `/`: lists both pages. Vue Router history mode; `dist/` served as a static SPA falls back to index.html (checked: `/nope` → 200 with `vite preview`).

## WebKit pieces used most
Blocks `platform/create/create-hub`, `shells/console`, `platform/view/table-view`. Components: `GlobalHeader`, `Sidebar` + `Menu`, `SearchTrigger` + `Command`, `PageHeader`, `Card`, `EmptyState`, `Button`, `IconButton`, `Tooltip`, `Input`, `ScrollArea`, `TableRoot` + `useCollection` + `Table.CellLink` / `CellTime` / `CellActions`, `Tag`, `StatusIndicator`, `Avatar`, `Brand`, `Breadcrumb`, `Link`, `WebkitProvider`. Icons: `ai-*` product icons, `ai-cor` framework marks. CLI: `init`, `search`, `view`, `add --with-guidelines`, `diff`, `check`, `doctor`.

## Top 5 problems with WebKit (by impact)
1. **TypeScript build fails out of the box** (high): on a fresh `create-vite vue-ts` app, `vue-tsc -b` can't resolve any `@aziontech/webkit/<name>` import (its exports point at raw `.vue` files), can't type `@aziontech/icons`, and the copied blocks are JS SFCs (TS7016). The README says `vue-tsc` "checks it under strict", which isn't true here. I needed `allowJs`, a hand-written `env.d.ts`, and had to keep my own SFCs as plain JS, because `webkit check` flags a `@aziontech/webkit/*` type shim as an unknown import.
2. **The tooling `init` installs breaks itself** (medium): the ESLint and stylelint configs don't ignore `dist/`, so after the first build the husky pre-commit hook fails with 526 errors in WebKit's own compiled output. The comment ban also rejects Vite's scaffold comment. `init` also needs a git repo before `npm install` and pins devDeps to `latest`.
3. **Skills contradict the real console** (medium): `webkit-tables` forbids a separate Author column, wants one chip per row, and wants stacked cards on narrow screens. The reference has Last Editor + Deployed columns, two chips, and a sideways-scrolling table on iPhone. The copy rules (no em dash, "select" not "choose") also conflict with the console's own copy.
4. **Missing assets and undocumented behaviour** (medium): there is no coloured Azion mark in `@aziontech/icons` and nothing maps a product name to its icon. The table-view block hot-links real photos from `ca.slack-edge.com`. `StatusIndicator` with `loading` adds its own "…" without documenting it, so "Building..." rendered as "Building......".
5. **Dependency and doc drift** (medium/low): webkit 5.12.0 asks for `@aziontech/theme ^4`, but the supplied theme is 5.2.2, so a second theme (4.3.1) gets nested and `doctor` doesn't notice. `webkit-usage` says to `import '@aziontech/theme'`, while CLAUDE.md says to import `webkit.css` instead. A skill example puts a colour class on `<Button>`, which the invariants forbid. `Link` ignores slot text, and `check` doesn't report block drift even though `diff` shows it.

What worked very well: `webkit search` found the exact block for both screens on the first try, and both blocks rendered almost the same as the references before I changed any content.

## Build
`npm run build` (`vue-tsc -b && vite build`) **passes**; `npx eslint .`, `stylelint` and `npx @aziontech/webkit check` pass (0 errors; 1 warning about `latest`-pinned devDeps).
